title: Prepare your Oracle database
summary: Set up a local Oracle Free database and a separate reading_app user. Learn the difference between an administrator and the API account.
introduction: A database is a place for keeping organised records. First we need a running Oracle database. Then we make a small, separate workspace for our book app. An adult, teacher or computer administrator can help with the installation.
learningObjectives: Choose the correct Oracle database service
Create a separate local learning account
Keep administrator credentials out of the API

blocks.text: Install or use a local learning database

Use [Oracle AI Database 26ai Free](https://www.oracle.com/database/free/get-started/) and follow the instructions for your operating system. Download from Oracle, extract the installer and record the connection details it shows. Keep the administrator password private.

The native Windows installer needs a supported Windows edition and administrator access. Windows Home is not supported by that installer. If your computer is not supported, use a compatible Linux machine or a teacher-provided learning database. Do not remove an existing database just to follow this lesson.

These lessons use the local address localhost:1521/FREEPDB1. **localhost** means this computer. **1521** is the database listener port, like a numbered door. **FREEPDB1** is the application database service inside the Free installation.

blocks.title: Check your actual service name
blocks.text: FREE is the root service, not the workspace we want. Older Oracle XE installations often use XEPDB1. Use the service shown by your own installation; changing the host to Docker does not change the service name.
Open a terminal in the extracted dotnet-oracle-backend folder. SQL*Plus is Oracle's command tool. It will ask for the administrator password without putting it in this command.

If the command is not found, use the full path to sqlplus.exe under your Oracle installation's bin folder, or an installed Oracle SQL client. In PowerShell, put & before a quoted executable path. The exact folder depends on your installation.

blocks.title: Inside SQL*Plus, from the sample root

blocks.text: SHOW CON_NAME should say FREEPDB1. Stop if it says CDB$ROOT; reconnect using the application service. The script asks you to choose a password for reading_app. Choose 12 to 30 characters using only letters, numbers, ! or _ for this practice script. These characters avoid SQL*Plus quoting surprises.

The script creates reading_app, gives it a small 10 MB space allowance and lets it connect and create its first table. This user is separate from SYSTEM. Do not use the administrator account in your API.
A **schema** is the group of database objects owned by a user. The reading_app schema will own our book table. No real school or personal records are needed; we use made-up book titles.

blocks.title: Run setup once
blocks.text: The script creates a new user. If Oracle says the user already exists, check whether it is your earlier practice account. Do not drop another person's user or data.
Write down only the host, port, service and username. Leave out both passwords. Point to the part of the address that names the application database.
